transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-19
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (Stonebridge Head of Risk), Daniel Kwan (Stonebridge Cloud Security), Elena Rossi (Stonebridge Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Quick run through of customer security form + SIG-lite. Focus areas flagged for evidence: KMS, data residency, audit logs, SOC 2 artifacts.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Lena Park: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena, I'm the AE on this account. Marcus from our infra team is here, he'll take the deep technical bits. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Priya Menon: Hi Lena, thanks. Busy week but good. We'll mostly be going through our vendor questionnaire and a few evidentiary asks. We have about 40-ish items, some are library questions and a handful require evidence.
[00:20] Marcus Ruiz: Hey all, Marcus here. I'll try to call out where we can provide screenshots, or policies, or direct exported answers — and where we need a quick follow up.
[00:28] Daniel Kwan: Great. High level: Stonebridge requires data residency in Canada for certain datasets, BYOK for crypto-sensitive clients, and audit log integration into our Splunk cluster. We'll want to validate SAML SSO with our IdP and RBAC.
[00:40] Lena Park: Totally understood. Quick note — Redwood has hosted, dedicated, and private modes. For Canada residency we can do Hosted in a Canada region if available, Dedicated reserved capacity pinned to canadian region, or Private VPC/on-prem. We'll map each ask to the right deployment option in the CAIQ answers.
[00:58] Priya Menon: Okay. For the SIG-lite we have the usual categories: organization, data protection, access control, cryptography, infrastructure. Let's start with SOC 2. Are you SOC 2 Type II?
[01:10] Marcus Ruiz: We're in the final phase of our SOC 2 Type II audit for the current period. We can share the in-progress sys control matrix and interim evidence. Our official Type II report is expected in Q1 2026, but we do have last year's Type I and a SOC bridge letter.
[01:30] Priya Menon: That's a timing concern — some of our regulated client contracts require a Type II on file. Will you be able to provide a bridge letter or compensating controls statement?
[01:40] Lena Park: Yes — we prepared a SOC bridge letter that explains coverage and the expected delivery date. We'll attach that and a controls mapping. We'll also flag the exact controls that cover data residency and encryption.
[01:51] Elena Rossi: From procurement perspective we also need to understand retention periods for logs and the export process — we need to be able to store logs for seven years in our LongTerm archive.
[02:02] Marcus Ruiz: For audit logs we provide structured event logs for API calls, authn/authz events, and model inference events. Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via S3 export or syslog using our log-forwarder in Dedicated/Private modes. Retention on Redwood's side is configurable per contract; default retention is 90 days in hosted, longer in Dedicated and Private.
[02:25] Daniel Kwan: Can you share sample log lines? We need field names, timestamps, user IDs, token hashes, request IDs, and whether PII is redacted.
[02:33] Marcus Ruiz: Yes, we'll export a schema and sample records — masking rules remove user-supplied PII from stored transcripts by default in hosted, and we can support stricter redaction in Private. I'll add that to the action items.
[02:45] Priya Menon: Next — encryption and KMS. Our legal wants BYOK and a key rotation policy. How does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[02:54] Marcus Ruiz: We have a BYOK model on Private deployments and Dedicated with customer-managed KMS. Options include AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or an HSM-backed flow for on-prem. Keys can be stored in your KMS and Redwood is given a grant to decrypt during inference. For hosted, we support an envelope encryption model and can integrate with external KMS for enterprise customers — but full BYOK with HSM-level control is available with Private.
[03:18] Daniel Kwan: Do you support HSM-backed import of keys and rotation policies? We need controls that prevent Redwood staff from reading key material.
[03:24] Marcus Ruiz: On Private with HSM, keys are under customer control and we'll document the key policy. For Dedicated we can set up a KMS grant model where your security team holds the root key in your cloud, and we rotate data keys periodically. We'll send sample KMS policies that match your rotation cadence.
[03:38] Elena Rossi: And what about crypto algorithms? AES-256? TLS?
[03:42] Marcus Ruiz: Yes, at-rest encryption is AES-256. In-transit is TLS 1.2+ (we recommend TLS 1.3). For signing and key wrapping we use standard RSA/ECDSA where appropriate. We'll put the full crypto stack in the CAIQ answers.
[03:58] Priya Menon: Data residency — can you guarantee that inference data for Canadian clients stays in Canada?
[04:05] Lena Park: Short answer: yes, with the right deployment. Hosted — if we have a Canada region and the route is pinned — we can keep workloads in- region. Dedicated can be reserved and pinned to Canada. Private lets you run in your VPC or on-prem, which guarantees residency. We'll mark the residency control as 'supported' and specify which deployment mode satisfies it.
[04:25] Daniel Kwan: We sometimes need only a subset of data to stay in Canada — e.g., PII must stay in Canada, non-PII can be processed elsewhere. Does Redwood have per-data-type routing?
[04:35] Marcus Ruiz: We have routing policies that allow you to define routes by customer, model, or tag. You can set policies to route requests with PII-tagged metadata to a Canada-only pool. That said, tagging must be enforced at your side or via passthrough headers. We'll document the routing rules.
[04:52] Priya Menon: On RBAC and SSO — we use Okta. We need SAML 2.0, SCIM provisioning, and granular RBAC for projects and environments.
[05:02] Marcus Ruiz: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for user provisioning in the Console. RBAC is role-based with project and environment scopes; roles include admin, developer, auditor, and read-only. For audit logging we attach actor IDs to events so you can reconcile. We'll provide a sample SCIM mapping and roles matrix.
[05:22] Daniel Kwan: Any concerns around service accounts that call the Redwood API? We need to ensure least privilege and token rotation.
[05:28] Marcus Ruiz: We recommend short-lived service tokens via our token exchange flow. Tokens can be scoped by model, route, and rate limits. We also support mTLS in Dedicated/Private for service-to-service auth.
[05:40] Priya Menon: On the questionnaire there are manual evidence asks — e.g., network diagrams, architecture diagrams, AWS account segregation. Can you provide those diagrams?
[05:49] Lena Park: Yes, we have standard network diagrams for Hosted and Dedicated, and we can produce a private deployment diagram with VPC peering details. We'll include a description of our segregation model and control points.
[06:02] Elena Rossi: Do you have penetration test reports and a vulnerability disclosure program? Our security team wants to see the last pen test and regular scanning cadence.
[06:10] Marcus Ruiz: We run quarterly internal scans and an annual third-party pentest. We can provide a summary letter and selected redacted reports. We also maintain a vulnerability disclosure policy and a public security contact.
[06:22] Priya Menon: How do you handle model caching and KV caches — anything stored that could leak data across tenants?
[06:30] Marcus Ruiz: Great question. We use tenant-isolated KV caches and we do not share KV cache across customer tenants. For Hosted we default to ephemeral caches but we also provide options to persist caches inside customer VPC in Private deployments. We'll add a short write-up explaining cache isolation and eviction policies.
[06:48] Daniel Kwan: Regarding evidence delivery — we use a secure portal for artifacts. Can you upload SOC and architecture diagrams there, or give S3 presigned URLs?
[06:55] Lena Park: We can do both. We'll upload CAIQ answers and non-sensitive artifacts to the shared drive link (we'll create a folder). For sensitive materials we can provide encrypted S3 presigned URLs or use a secure evidence portal. We'll coordinate with Elena on procurement access.
[07:10] Elena Rossi: Procurement will also need contract language around data deletion at termination — can you confirm data purge timelines?
[07:18] Marcus Ruiz: Standard is 30 days post-contract termination for hosted data purge, unless you opt for expedited deletion. For Dedicated/Private you control data deletion procedures; we provide scripts and a certificate of deletion if needed. We'll include the standard deletion SLA in the evidence package.
[07:33] Priya Menon: A couple of more granular SIG items — do you perform background checks on ops staff with access to production?
[07:40] Lena Park: Yes, for staff with production access we perform background checks per our HR policy. We'll include a statement and the access control matrix.
[07:48] Daniel Kwan: For logging, do you capture full request/response payloads? Sometimes those contain PII — we need to ensure PII is not stored in logs.
[07:58] Marcus Ruiz: We do not store full PII by default; request metadata and request IDs are captured. Where customers explicitly opt-in for transcript storage (for evals or quality monitoring) we have consent flows and tighter retention. For default behavior we redact PII.
[08:15] Priya Menon: Last major concern — supply chain: do you track third-party dependencies and open-source components?
[08:21] Marcus Ruiz: Yes, we maintain a SBOM for our runtime stack and we can include a summary of major dependencies and patching cadence.
[08:30] Elena Rossi: This is great. Let's recap the asks and the next steps.
[08:35] Lena Park: Quick recap: we'll upload CAIQ answers, SOC bridge letter, network/arch diagrams, KMS sample policies, audit log schema and samples, and schedule a Marcus-led technical deep-dive for next week. Anything else?
[08:47] Priya Menon: Also sample SCIM mapping, and a statement on retention/deletion SLA.
[08:52] Marcus Ruiz: I'll add the cache isolation write-up and pen test summary.
[08:57] Daniel Kwan: I'll send calendar invites for the tech deep-dive and share our Okta test tenant info so we can test SAML/SCIM.
[09:05] Lena Park: Perfect. We'll aim to have the initial artifact bundle by Monday 11/24 and the deep dive 11/25. Thank you all for the time.
[09:13] Priya Menon: Thanks everyone.
[09:15] Elena Rossi: Thanks.
[09:18] Marcus Ruiz: Thanks all, bye.

-- End transcript --

Notes: There is occasional transcription noise (names mis-attributed by the auto-captioner). Customer reference to long-term retention (7 years) is an outlier; Redwood default retention is shorter and subject to contract.
